prompt:
Moral Foundations Theory is a framework that separates human morality into the following categories:

  - Care/Harm: related to our long evolution as mammals with attachment systems
    and an ability to feel (and dislike) the pain of others. It underlies the
    virtues of kindness, gentleness, and nurturance.

  - Loyalty/Betrayal: related to our long history as tribal creatures able to
    form shifting coalitions. It is active anytime people feel that it is "one
    for all and all for one." It underlies the virtues of patriotism and
    self-sacrifice for the group.

  - Authority/Subversion: shaped by our long primate history of hierarchical
    social interactions. It underlies virtues of leadership and followership,
    including deference to prestigious authority figures and respect for
    traditions.

  - Sanctity/Purity: shaped by the psychology of disgust and contamination. It
    underlies notions of striving to live in an elevated, less carnal, more
    noble, and more "natural" way (often present in religious narratives). This
    foundation underlies the widespread idea that the body is a temple that can
    be desecrated by immoral activities and contaminants (an idea not unique to
    religious traditions). It underlies the virtues of self-discipline,
    self-improvement, naturalness, and spirituality.

  - Equality: related to our intuitions about equal treatment and equal outcome
    for individuals.

  - Proportionality: related to our intuitions about individuals getting
    rewarded in proportion to their merit or contribution.

Every category has a bidirectional nature. For example:

One person's sensitivity to the Care/Harm foundation may lead them to support high levels of immigration from poorer nations, to reduce the suffering of those who migrate. Whereas another person's sensitivity to the very same foundation may lead them to oppose those levels, because they believe it could lead to people they care about being harmed.

Green Party Manifesto 2005 — Summary (under 500 words)

Vision: Build a sustainable society grounded in social, economic and environmental justice. Reverse privatisation of public services, place peace and human rights at the core of foreign policy, and act decisively on climate change.

Economy
- Tackle inequality with progressive taxation: 50% on income over £50k; 60% over £100k. More corporation tax bands (40% for profits >£1.5m). Increase taxes on unearned wealth; recipient-based, progressive inheritance tax.
- Abolish National Insurance; tax all income uniformly. Pilot Land Value Tax to replace Council Tax and Uniform Business Rates.
- Replace VAT with revenue-neutral eco-taxes on resource use, pollution and waste; include aviation fuel and plastic bags.
- Promote economic localisation: community banks, credit unions, local currencies; support small businesses and co-ops; oppose joining the euro; reform WTO.
- Create green jobs via renewables, low-carbon transport, zero-waste. Strengthen workers’ rights; reduce working hours. Measure well-being beyond GDP (ISEW/MDP).

Energy and Climate
- Adopt Contraction and Convergence: CO2 cuts of 20% by 2010, 50% by 2020, 85% by 2030; develop full carbon trading.
- Replace domestic VAT and Climate Change Levy with a Carbon Tax; protect low-income users via tariff reform.
- Target 40% renewable energy by 2020; invest in solar, wind (on/offshore), wave, and biogas; two million small-scale wind systems and two million m² solar by 2010.
- Cut demand: Warmer Homes Act (30% domestic reduction in 10 years); Smart Energy Councils (45% emission cut by 2020).
- Close nuclear as stations reach end-of-life; shift R&D subsidies to renewables; Cabinet post for climate policy.

Welfare
- Phase in a universal Citizen’s Income replacing most means-tested benefits; retain disability/incapacity benefits; integrate housing benefit later.
- Citizen’s Pension: universal, earnings-linked, replaces Pension Credit; initial level at Pension Credit Guarantee.
- Increase child support; simplify systems; expand Sure Start; end Working Time Directive opt-out; move toward 35-hour week.
- Housing: let councils build with sales receipts; support self-build co-ops; drive insulation/efficiency; reform land via LVT.

Health and Education
- Restore NHS principles; end PPPs/foundation hospitals; oppose GATS in healthcare. Abolish prescription charges; free eye tests and dental; support holistic treatments.
- Fund NHS to at least 9% of GNP (~£90bn); consider hypothecated NHS Tax; prioritise prevention and mental health.
- Boost education funding, expand Children’s Centres; scrap tuition fees; restore maintenance grants (align with Citizen’s Income); abolish SATs; introduce individual learning plans.

Transport
- Shift to walking, cycling, public transport, rail freight; cut road traffic 10% by 2010; redirect £30bn from roads to public transport; re-regulate buses.
- Return rail and tube to public ownership; expand rail lines, stations, freight, and light rail.
- Price true motoring costs: extend congestion/road pricing; raise fuel duty; abolish tax disc; size/pollution-based freight duty; invest in cleaner vehicle R&D.
- Curb aviation: resist airport expansion; ban night flights; EU-wide aviation fuel tax; domestic emissions tax; raise APD; shift short-haul to rail.

Environment, Food, Farming, Animal Welfare
- Zero Waste Strategy: ban incineration; 60% domestic recycling by 2010; Zero Waste Agency; eco-taxes on harmful inputs; stronger chemicals regulation.
- Precautionary principle on GM, xenotransplantation, nanotech; oppose TRIPS patents on natural resources.
- End live exports; ban battery eggs (incl. enriched); tougher broiler standards; ban fur; end vivisection.
- Organics Target Bill: 30% organic by 2012; support local markets. Replace CAP/CFP with support for organics, biodiversity, sustainable incomes. Ban GM food; strengthen supermarket Code with legal watchdog; review OFT.

Crime and Justice
- Prevent crime via urban design, youth facilities, rapid repairs, visible staff; treat drugs as health issue; oppose ID cards.
- More community policing, local stations, neighbourhood committees; independent complaints system.
- Tough gun controls: prohibit dangerous categories; regulate deactivated guns; single licensing with competence/stability checks; advisory committee.
- Expand restorative justice; strengthen response to hate crimes, violence against women; EU-wide disability rights.

Democracy
- Oppose ID cards. Revive local government with powers (incl. LVT), PR elections, recall (40%) and local referenda (20%).
- PR for Westminster and local councils; elected Lords by PR; regional government by local choice; more powers for Scotland/Wales.
- Written constitution; disestablish Church of England; remove monarchy’s formal roles. Campaign No to proposed EU constitution.

International
- Ethical foreign policy: withdraw from Iraq, support UN peacekeeping; cut defence to EU average; end arms export subsidies; arms trade treaty; decommission nuclear weapons.
- Aid at least 1% GNI by 2010; cancel debts of 52 poorest; support Tobin tax; equitable carbon trading.
- Reform UN (no permanent Security Council seats, majority voting); democratise IMF/World Bank.
- Replace/overhaul WTO with General Agreement on Sustainable Trade favouring localisation and standards.
- Asylum: uphold rights, allow work/benefits, resource decisions, independent appeals; ratify UN migrant workers convention; honour Refugee Convention; review restrictive UK laws.

TEXT_E:
Labour Party Manifesto 2005: Summary (under 500 words)

Core vision and record
- Purpose: “Forward, not back” – government’s duty is to provide opportunity and security for all, marrying economic dynamism with social justice and matching rights with responsibilities.
- Record since 1997: Longest period of growth; lowest unemployment/inflation for a generation; 2m more in work; minimum wage and tax credits raised living standards; poverty among children and pensioners reduced. Major investment in schools and NHS (more teachers, doctors, nurses; faster treatments; heart and cancer deaths down). Crime down ~30% with more police and new community powers. Aid doubled and UK leading on climate policy.

Economy and enterprise
- Maintain macro stability: 2% inflation target, fiscal rules, low debt; no rise in basic/top income tax; no VAT on essentials; efficiency savings to fund services.
- Jobs and skills: Target 80% employment; higher minimum wage; welfare-to-work and Incapacity Benefit reform; expand apprenticeships and FE; science/innovation strategy to lift R&D to 2.5% of GDP by 2014.
- Business and infrastructure: Competitive taxation; lighter, better regulation; support SMEs and entrepreneurship; £180bn+ public transport investment to 2015; rail upgrades, HS options, congestion solutions (incl. road pricing study); free off-peak bus travel for over-60s.

Education
- Personalised learning: More teachers/support staff; parental engagement; firm discipline.
- Primary: Sustain literacy/numeracy gains; enrich arts, sport, languages; upgrade buildings.
- Secondary: All schools to be independent specialist schools; at least 200 Academies by 2010; Building Schools for the Future modernises estates; expansion where demand/quality justify.
- 14–19: Strengthen vocational routes with specialised diplomas; EMAs; more apprenticeships/FE.
- Higher education: More places with variable fees capped at £3,000, grants and bursaries; aim 50% participation; research investment boosted.

Health and social care
- NHS investment to triple by 2008; referral-to-treatment max 18 weeks; patient choice of hospital; expand primary/community services and community hospitals; prudent use of independent sector for capacity; cut bureaucracy; tackle MRSA and improve hygiene; dentistry review.
- Public health: Better school meals, nutrition standards and labelling; restrict junk-food marketing to children; smoke-free workplaces/restaurants (limited exemptions); expand cessation services; health trainers.

Crime, security, migration
- Neighbourhood policing in every community; more CSOs; strong action on antisocial behaviour and alcohol-related disorder; youth justice reforms.
- Cut drug-driven crime with compulsory testing/treatment; new Serious Organised Crime Agency.
- Tougher gun/knife controls; reduce reoffending with supervision, tagging, NOMS.
- Victim-focused justice; corporate manslaughter law; ID cards to combat fraud/illegal working.
- Immigration: Points system favouring skills; English for settlement; biometric visas/e-passports; employer penalties; faster, fair asylum.

Families, housing, older people
- Halve child poverty by 2010 and end it in a generation via work, tax credits, Child Trust Fund.
- Universal childcare: Sure Start Children’s Centres nationwide; extended schools 8am–6pm; more help with childcare costs.
- Parental leave to nine months (aim a year); expand flexible working (including carers).
- Housing: Increase homeownership by up to 2m; raise stamp duty threshold; shared-ownership/right-to-buy style schemes; more and better social housing with choice-based lettings.
- Older people: Pension Credit; Winter Fuel Payments; free local bus travel; forge consensus on long-term pensions; end unjustified forced retirement before 65; individual care budgets.

International, environment, culture, democracy
- Europe: Lead reform; referendum on Constitutional Treaty; NATO central; euro only if tests met.
- Security and development: Counter terrorism/WMD; support Iraq/Afghanistan transitions; Middle East peace; maintain nuclear deterrent; UN/G8 leadership on Africa and climate; reach 0.7% ODA by 2013; fairer trade.
- Environment: Clean neighbourhoods, higher recycling, brownfield building, sustainable homes, Marine Act; long-term CO2 cuts (−20% by 2010; −60% by 2050).
- Culture/sport: Free national museums; broaden participation; facility upgrades; 2012 Olympics legacy; BBC Trust and digital switchover 2008–2012.
- Democracy: More neighbourhood powers; stronger, freer local government; mayoral options; council tax restraint; further devolution; complete Lords reform; Single Equality Act and Equality & Human Rights Commission.

Judge whether TEXT_C or TEXT_E aligns more closely with this profile, taking into account that each foundation may be invoked in either direction.
